The Surface Water Temperature layer is a polygon layer that outlines water temperature classifications for reaches in the Conservation Halton watershed.  The layer is based on temperature data collected at numerous points throughout the watershed over a number of years through the use of temperature dataloggers.  The individual temperatures are analyzed in combination with the air temperatures following the protocol of Chu et al. (2008).  The resulting classifications include cold, cold-cool, cool, cool-warm and warm.  These classifications align with preferred temperatures for a number of Ontario fish species and as such can help provide direction as to the habitat conditions and potential presence of a variety of Ontario freshwater fish species. 

Note-reach classifications are based on individual point data across a stream reach.  Due to the presence of localized changes in conditions (e.g. springs, impoundments etc.) individual temperatures at specific locations may differ then mapped reaches.
